game: DEN@KC Week 1 2026, kickoff 2026-09-14 20:15 ET, KC -2.5, total 42.5, outdoors

script.base: Market prices a close outdoor game: KC -2.5 at home, total 42.5, implied KC 22.5 and DEN 20.0. KC leads by about a score late, pace stays moderate, both QBs stay in it, and neither backfield is in a pure clock-kill or abandon-the-run script. Not a shootout and not a blowout.
script.flip1: KC jumps up by two scores early, Kenneth Walker (rush line 66.5) and Kareem Hunt grind the clock, and DEN abandons the run so J.K. Dobbins (78.5) and RJ Harvey (30.5) rush yards die while Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Jaylen Waddle and Evan Engram targets rise.
script.flip2: DEN hangs or leads and the 42.5 total slides into a slog or a KC pass-chase. Josh Simmons already out, KC rush efficiency falls further, and Rashee Rice / Xavier Worthy have to win through the air while Hunt's carries shrink.

injury_fallout: nflverse pre-game injury report only: KC S Chamarri Conner Out (knee), KC T Josh Simmons Out (back). No DEN outs in the pack. Conner out is a missing safety, so DEN vertical options (Sutton recyds 62.5, Waddle 51.5, Franklin 35.5) are the skill players who gain, not KC's own receivers. Simmons out raises pressure on KC, lowers Walker/Hunt rush efficiency, pushes quick throws toward Travis Kelce and the RBs, and cuts deep yards for Worthy (38.5) and Rice (65.5). Final inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are not in the pack.

Total 42.5 is moderate-low, so this is an unders and run-lean environment, not a volume-over slate. Blowout flag is off, so starter snap risk is low. A mild KC lead late helps the lead back's carries more than the complement (Hunt, rush line 34.5 vs Walker 66.5).

edge_players.edge_sentence: Kareem Hunt is priced as the complement behind Kenneth Walker's 66.5 rush line, his last four rush games were 12, 2, 38 and 14, and KC is without tackle Josh Simmons, so he does not need 34.5 rush yards in a 22.5-point KC script.
edge_players.must_be_true: Walker is active and takes the early-down carries the 66.5 line implies, Hunt stays in that complementary rush role, Simmons remains out, and the game stays inside a one-score script rather than a Hunt-only grind.
edge_players.kills_it: Walker is not installed in week 1 (2025 logs may be another team) and Hunt inherits the early-down load, or DEN's uncharted run defense is soft enough that a complement still clears 35, as his 38-yard game already did.

market_rung_price: Kareem Hunt rush yards under 34.5, main line only. No book price, no alt rung, no anchor. No short-priced alt. No stake; this backtest does not place a bet.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and Hunt under 34.5 lost because Walker, whose 2025 logs may be another team, was not the week-1 bellcow the 66.5 line assumed. Hunt got a full early-down share in a one-score grind, DEN's uncharted run fits were light, and his 38-yard game already shows 34.5 does not require a featured role. Simmons being out did not cap the yards if the carries simply moved from Walker to Hunt. No saved weather check could rescue an outdoor under either.
slip_story: Low-total, slight-home-favorite unders. One leg only: Hunt rush under, which needs KC not handing the complement 35 rush yards. Do not pair with DEN receiver overs (those need the Conner-out pass script) or with Walker rush over (same backfield, opposite carry assumption). No TDs, no receptions, no parlay.
